svg.title: Matching a name to a stored entity
svg.desc: How Graphiti decides whether a name in a new message is an entity it already has. Names that are not stored exactly are compared by the cosine similarity of their embeddings, and only stored entities scoring at least 0.6 are shown to the model. Left, 'Anton's sister Lena' in July: Anton's sister scores 0.882 and Anton 0.756, both are shown, and the model says it is Anton's sister. Right, plain 'Lena' two messages later: Lena's partner Jonas 0.787 and Anton 0.608 are shown; Assistant 0.5997 and Anton's sister 0.5949 fall just under the floor. The model rightly says Lena is neither Jonas nor Anton, so a new, second node for Lena is made, and 'Lena cannot eat shellfish' is stored on it.
svg.text: Matching a name to a stored entity
A name that is not stored exactly is compared with every stored entity's name by embedding. Only those scoring at least
0.6 are shown to the model, which decides if one of them is the same thing. The rest are never considered.
“my sister Lena is coming back in the autumn”
The model is shown the two over the floor and picks Anton's sister.
“Lena can't eat shellfish, and Jonas is coeliac”
The model is shown Jonas and Anton, and rightly says Lena is neither.
A first name alone carries little meaning for an embedding: “Lena” is about as close to “Berlin” as to “Anton's sister”. The stored node kept its old
name, “Anton's sister”, when it was matched to “Anton's sister Lena” (0.779 against “Lena”), so the name that would have matched was never
